sanskrit: imaṃ ca samupālambhaṃ tvatto rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śṛṇuyād yadi kalyāṇi kṛtsnaṃ jahyāt sa jīvitam
english: If King Yudhiṣṭhira were to hear this reproach of yours, O auspicious one, he would entirely abandon his life.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayo vā suśroṇi yamau vā tanumadhyame lokāntaragateṣv eṣu nāhaṃ śakṣyāmi jīvitum
english: Or if Dhanaṃjaya, O lovely-hipped one, or the twins were to pass to another world, I could not continue living, O slender-waisted one.

sanskrit: sukanyā nāma śāryātī bhārgavaṃ cyavanaṃ vane valmīkabhūtaṃ śāmyantam anvapadyata bhāminī
english: Sukanyā, daughter of Śāryāta, a proud and beautiful woman, followed the sage Cyavana of the Bhṛgu lineage into the forest, where he sat in meditation, having become an anthill.

sanskrit: nāḍāyanī cendrasenā rūpeṇa yadi te śrutā patim anvacarad vṛddhaṃ purā varṣasahasriṇam
english: And if you have heard of Nāḍāyanī and Indrasenā, radiant in beauty — she followed her aged husband, who had lived for a thousand years.

sanskrit: duhitā janakasyāpi vaidehī yadi te śrutā patim anvacarat sītā mahāraṇyanivāsinam
english: And if you have heard of Vaidehī, daughter of Janaka — Sītā followed her husband Rāma who dwelt in the great forest.

sanskrit: rakṣasā nigrahaṃ prāpya rāmasya mahiṣī priyā kliśyamānāpi suśroṇī rāmam evānvapadyata
english: Though seized and oppressed by a demon, Rāma's beloved queen, O lovely-hipped one, followed Rāma alone even in her affliction.

sanskrit: lopāmudrā tathā bhīru vayorūpasamanvitā agastyam anvayād dhitvā kāmān sarvān amānuṣān
english: So too Lopāmudrā, O timid one, though endowed with youth and beauty, followed Agastya, abandoning all superhuman pleasures.

sanskrit: yathaitāḥ kīrtitā nāryo rūpavatyaḥ pativratāḥ tathā tvam api kalyāṇi sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ
english: Just as these women, praised for their beauty and devotion to their husbands, are celebrated, so too are you, O auspicious one, endowed with all virtues.

sanskrit: mādīrghaṃ kṣama kālaṃ tvaṃ māsam adhyardhasaṃmitam pūrṇe trayodaśe varṣe rājño rājñī bhaviṣyasi
english: Bear this long period patiently — it amounts to only a month and a half more; when the thirteenth year is complete, you shall be queen of the king again.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca ārtayaitan mayā bhīma kṛtaṃ bāṣpavimokṣaṇam apārayantyā duḥkhāni na rājānam upālabhe
english: Draupadī said: It is out of distress, O Bhīma, that I have shed these tears, being unable to bear my sufferings — I do not reproach the king.

sanskrit: vimuktena vyatītena bhīmasena mahābala pratyupasthitakālasya kāryasyānantaro bhava
english: O Bhīmasena of great might, now that the period of concealment has passed and the time for action is at hand, be ready to act without delay.

sanskrit: mameha bhīma kaikeyī rūpābhibhavaśaṅkayā nityam udvijate rājā kathaṃ neyād imām iti
english: Here, O Bhīma, the princess Kaikeyī always torments me out of fear that I might surpass her in beauty — the king constantly worries about how to keep her satisfied.

sanskrit: tasyā viditvā taṃ bhāvaṃ svayaṃ cānṛtadarśanaḥ kīcako 'yaṃ suduṣṭātmā sadā prārthayate hi mām
english: And knowing her feelings, this Kīcaka, wicked-souled and himself of crooked vision, always importunes me.

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ kupitā bhīma punaḥ kopaṃ niyamya ca abruvaṃ kāmasaṃmūḍham ātmānaṃ rakṣa kīcaka
english: Angry at him, O Bhīma, yet restraining my anger again and again, I spoke to that one blinded by desire: 'Protect yourself, Kīcaka.'

sanskrit: gandharvāṇām ahaṃ bhāryā pañcānāṃ mahiṣī priyā te tvāṃ nihanyur durdharṣāḥ śūrāḥ sāhasakāriṇaḥ
english: 'I am the wife of the Gandharvas, the beloved queen of five of them — those fierce, bold warriors will slay you.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa duṣṭātmā kīcakaḥ pratyuvāca ha nāhaṃ bibhemi sairandhri gandharvāṇāṃ śucismite
english: Thus addressed, that wicked-souled Kīcaka replied: 'I do not fear the Gandharvas, O Sairandhrī of bright smile.'

sanskrit: śataṃ sahasram api vā gandharvāṇām ahaṃ raṇe samāgataṃ haniṣyāmi tvaṃ bhīru kuru me kṣaṇam
english: 'Even a hundred or a thousand Gandharvas assembled in battle I would slay — O timid one, grant me even one moment of your company.'

sanskrit: ity ukte cābruvaṃ sūtaṃ kāmāturam ahaṃ punaḥ na tvaṃ pratibalas teṣāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ yaśasvinām
english: When he spoke thus, I again told that charioteer's son consumed by desire: 'You are no match for those glorious Gandharvas.'

sanskrit: dharme sthitāsmi satataṃ kulaśīlasamanvitā necchāmi kaṃ cid vadhyantaṃ tena jīvasi kīcaka
english: 'I am always established in righteousness, endowed with noble lineage and virtue — I do not wish anyone to be slain, and that is why you still live, Kīcaka.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa duṣṭātmā prahasya svanavat tadā na tiṣṭhati sma sanmārge na ca dharmaṃ bubhūṣati
english: Thus addressed, that wicked-souled one laughed loudly then — he did not remain on the path of righteousness, nor did he desire to follow dharma.

sanskrit: pāpātmā pāpabhāvaś ca kāmarāgavaśānugaḥ avinītaś ca duṣṭātmā pratyākhyātaḥ punaḥ punaḥ darśane darśane hanyāt tathā jahyāṃ ca jīvitam
english: Evil-souled, evil-minded, enslaved to lust and passion, rude and wicked — though rejected again and again, he would torment me at every encounter, and so I would rather abandon my life.

sanskrit: tad dharme yatamānānāṃ mahān dharmo naśiṣyati samayaṃ rakṣamāṇānāṃ bhāryā vo na bhaviṣyati
english: Therefore, if you strive in dharma, great dharma will not perish for those who keep their vow — but if you do not protect your wife, she will no longer be yours.

sanskrit: bhāryāyāṃ rakṣyamāṇāyāṃ prajā bhavati rakṣitā prajāyāṃ rakṣyamāṇāyām ātmā bhavati rakṣitaḥ
english: When a wife is protected, progeny is protected; when progeny is protected, the self is protected.

sanskrit: vadatāṃ varṇadharmāṃś ca brāhmaṇānāṃ hi me śrutam kṣatriyasya sadā dharmo nānyaḥ śatrunibarhaṇāt
english: I have heard from Brahmins who expound the duties of the castes that the dharma of a Kṣatriya is always nothing other than the destruction of enemies.

sanskrit: paśyato dharmarājasya kīcako māṃ padāvadhīt tava caiva samakṣaṃ vai bhīmasena mahābala
english: In the sight of the king of dharma and before your very eyes, O mighty Bhīmasena, Kīcaka struck me with his foot.

sanskrit: tvayā hy ahaṃ paritrātā tasmād ghorāj jaṭāsurāt jayadrathaṃ tathaiva tvam ajaiṣīr bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: It was you who rescued me from that terrible demon Jaṭāsura; and likewise you conquered Jayadratha together with your brothers.

sanskrit: jahīmam api pāpaṃ tvaṃ yo 'yaṃ mām avamanyate kīcako rājavāllabhyāc chokakṛn mama bhārata
english: Slay this wretch too, O Bhārata, this Kīcaka who insults me, relying on the king's favor, and who causes me grief.

sanskrit: tam evaṃ kāmasaṃmattaṃ bhindhi kumbham ivāśmani yo nimittam anarthānāṃ bahūnāṃ mama bhārata
english: Smash him who is thus maddened by lust — smash him like a pot against a stone — for he is the cause of many calamities for me, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: taṃ cej jīvantam ādityaḥ prātar abhyudayiṣyati viṣam āloḍya pāsyāmi mā kīcakavaśaṃ gamam śreyo hi maraṇaṃ mahyaṃ bhīmasena tavāgrataḥ
english: If the sun rises tomorrow and he still lives, I will mix poison and drink it — I will not fall under Kīcaka's power; death before you, O Bhīmasena, is better for me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā prārudat kṛṣṇā bhīmasyoraḥ samāśritā bhīmaś ca tāṃ pariṣvajya mahat sāntvaṃ prayujya ca kīcakaṃ manasāgacchat sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇā wept, leaning against Bhīma's chest; and Bhīma, embracing her and offering great consolation, turned his mind to Kīcaka, licking the corners of his lips.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca tathā bhadre kariṣyāmi yathā tvaṃ bhīru bhāṣase adya taṃ sūdayiṣyāmi kīcakaṃ sahabāndhavam
english: Bhīmasena said: I shall do exactly as you say, O fortunate one, O timid lady — today I will slay Kīcaka along with all his kinsmen.

sanskrit: asyāḥ pradoṣe śarvaryāḥ kuruṣvānena saṃgamam duḥkhaṃ śokaṃ ca nirdhūya yājñaseni śucismite
english: At the early part of this night, O Yājñasenī of bright smile, shaking off your sorrow and grief, arrange a meeting with him.

sanskrit: yaiṣā nartanaśālā vai matsyarājena kāritā divātra kanyā nṛtyanti rātrau yānti yathāgṛham
english: There is the dance hall built by the king of Matsya — during the day young women dance there, at night they go to their homes.

sanskrit: tatrāsti śayanaṃ bhīru dṛḍhāṅgaṃ supratiṣṭhitam tatrāsya darśayiṣyāmi pūrvapretān pitāmahān
english: There is a bed there, O timid one, firm-framed and well set — there I will show him his forefathers who have gone before to the realm of the dead.

sanskrit: yathā ca tvāṃ na paśyeyuḥ kurvāṇāṃ tena saṃvidam kuryās tathā tvaṃ kalyāṇi yathā saṃnihito bhavet
english: Arrange matters, O auspicious one, so that no one sees you making this assignation with him, and so that I may be close at hand.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā tau kathayitvā tu bāṣpam utsṛjya duḥkhitau rātriśeṣaṃ tad atyugraṃ dhārayām āsatur hṛdā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to each other and shedding tears, the two of them, filled with grief, bore that terribly harsh remainder of the night in their hearts.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prātar utthāya kīcakaḥ gatvā rājakulāyaiva draupadīm idam abravīt
english: When that night had passed, Kīcaka rose at dawn and going directly to the royal household, spoke these words to Draupadī.

sanskrit: sabhāyāṃ paśyato rājñaḥ pātayitvā padāhanam na caivālabhathās trāṇam abhipannā balīyasā
english: 'In the assembly hall, before the king's eyes, I kicked you down, and yet you found no protection even when you appealed to one mightier than I.'

sanskrit: pravādena hi matsyānāṃ rājā nāmnāyam ucyate aham eva hi matsyānāṃ rājā vai vāhinīpatiḥ
english: 'For it is only by name that this one is called king of the Matsyas — I myself am truly the king of the Matsyas, the commander of the army.'

sanskrit: sā sukhaṃ pratipadyasva dāso bhīru bhavāmi te ahnāya tava suśroṇi śataṃ niṣkān dadāmy aham
english: 'Come willingly to me, O timid one — I shall become your slave; I will give you a hundred gold coins this very day, O lovely-hipped one.'

sanskrit: dāsīśataṃ ca te dadyāṃ dāsānām api cāparam rathaṃ cāśvatarīyuktam astu nau bhīru saṃgamaḥ
english: 'And I would give you a hundred maidservants, and male servants beyond that, and a chariot yoked with mules — O timid one, let there be a union between us.'

sanskrit: draupady uvāca ekaṃ me samayaṃ tv adya pratipadyasva kīcaka na tvāṃ sakhā vā bhrātā vā jānīyāt saṃgataṃ mayā
english: Draupadī said: Agree to one condition of mine today, Kīcaka — let no friend or brother of yours know that you have met with me.

sanskrit: avabodhād dhi bhītāsmi gandharvāṇāṃ yaśasvinām evaṃ me pratijānīhi tato 'haṃ vaśagā tava
english: For I am afraid of the glorious Gandharvas finding out; promise me this, and then I shall be yours to command.

sanskrit: kīcaka uvāca evam etat kariṣyāmi yathā suśroṇi bhāṣase eko bhadre gamiṣyāmi śūnyam āvasathaṃ tava
english: Kīcaka said: I will do exactly as you say, O lovely-hipped one; I shall go alone, O blessed one, to your empty dwelling.

sanskrit: samāgamārthaṃ rambhoru tvayā madanamohitaḥ yathā tvāṃ nāvabhotsyanti gandharvāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ
english: For the sake of union with you, O round-thighed one, I am maddened by desire — so that the Gandharvas of solar splendor will not discover you.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca yad idaṃ nartanāgāraṃ matsyarājena kāritam divātra kanyā nṛtyanti rātrau yānti yathāgṛham
english: Draupadī said: That dance hall which was built by the king of Matsya — during the day young women dance there, at night they go to their homes.

sanskrit: tamisre tatra gacchethā gandharvās tan na jānate tatra doṣaḥ parihṛto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Go there in the darkness — the Gandharvas do not know of it; the fault will be avoided there, without doubt.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam arthaṃ pratijalpantyāḥ kṛṣṇāyāḥ kīcakena ha divasārdhaṃ samabhavan māsenaiva samaṃ nṛpa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While Kṛṣṇā was speaking these words and Kīcaka was responding, O king, half a day passed — it seemed equal to an entire month.

sanskrit: kīcako 'tha gṛhaṃ gatvā bhṛśaṃ harṣapariplutaḥ sairandhrīrūpiṇaṃ mūḍho mṛtyuṃ taṃ nāvabuddhavān
english: Then Kīcaka went home, overwhelmed with joy — the fool did not perceive that what appeared to him as the Sairandhrī was in fact Death itself.

sanskrit: gandhābharaṇamālyeṣu vyāsaktaḥ sa viśeṣataḥ alaṃcakāra so ''tmānaṃ satvaraḥ kāmamohitaḥ
english: Engrossed especially in perfumes, ornaments, and garlands, he hastily adorned himself, blinded by desire.

sanskrit: tasya tat kurvataḥ karma kālo dīrgha ivābhavat anucintayataś cāpi tām evāyatalocanām
english: While he was doing this, time seemed very long to him, as he thought over and over of that long-eyed woman.

sanskrit: āsīd abhyadhikā cāsya śrīḥ śriyaṃ pramumukṣataḥ nirvāṇakāle dīpasya vartīm iva didhakṣataḥ
english: His splendor appeared even greater than usual — like a lamp's wick about to flare up at the moment of extinction, the splendor of one about to lose all splendor.

sanskrit: kṛtasaṃpratyayas tatra kīcakaḥ kāmamohitaḥ nājānād divasaṃ yāntaṃ cintayānaḥ samāgamam
english: With his mind made up about the meeting, Kīcaka, blinded by desire, did not notice the day passing as he brooded on the assignation.

sanskrit: tatas tu draupadī gatvā tadā bhīmaṃ mahānase upātiṣṭhata kalyāṇī kauravyaṃ patim antikāt
english: Then Draupadī, the auspicious one of Kuru lineage, went to the kitchen and approached her husband Bhīma closely.

sanskrit: tam uvāca sukeśāntā kīcakasya mayā kṛtaḥ saṃgamo nartanāgāre yathāvocaḥ paraṃtapa
english: With her beautiful hair ends, she spoke to him: 'I have arranged a meeting with Kīcaka in the dance hall, as you instructed me, O scorcher of foes.'

sanskrit: śūnyaṃ sa nartanāgāram āgamiṣyati kīcakaḥ eko niśi mahābāho kīcakaṃ taṃ niṣūdaya
english: 'That Kīcaka will come alone to the empty dance hall at night, O mighty-armed one — slay that Kīcaka.'

sanskrit: taṃ sūtaputraṃ kaunteya kīcakaṃ madadarpitam gatvā tvaṃ nartanāgāraṃ nirjīvaṃ kuru pāṇḍava
english: 'That son of a charioteer, Kīcaka, arrogant with pride — go to the dance hall, O son of Kuntī, and render him lifeless, O Pāṇḍava.'

sanskrit: darpāc ca sūtaputro 'sau gandharvān avamanyate taṃ tvaṃ praharatāṃ śreṣṭha naḍaṃ nāga ivoddhara
english: 'And that son of a charioteer out of arrogance insults the Gandharvas — uproot him, O best of warriors, as an elephant uproots a reed.'

sanskrit: aśru duḥkhābhibhūtāyā mama mārjasva bhārata ātmanaś caiva bhadraṃ te kuru mānaṃ kulasya ca
english: 'Wipe away the tears of me who am overcome with grief, O Bhārata — do what is good for yourself, and uphold the honor of our family.'

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca svāgataṃ te varārohe yan mā vedayase priyam na hy asya kaṃ cid icchāmi sahāyaṃ varavarṇini
english: Bhīmasena said: Welcome, O lovely-hipped one, is the glad news you bring me — I desire no helper at all for this task, O woman of excellent complexion.

sanskrit: yā me prītis tvayākhyātā kīcakasya samāgame hatvā hiḍimbaṃ sā prītir mamāsīd varavarṇini
english: The joy you have told me of — this meeting with Kīcaka — is the same joy I felt when I slew Hiḍimba, O woman of excellent complexion.

sanskrit: satyaṃ bhrātṝṃś ca dharmaṃ ca puraskṛtya bravīmi te kīcakaṃ nihaniṣyāmi vṛtraṃ devapatir yathā
english: Placing truth, my brothers, and dharma before me, I tell you truly: I will slay Kīcaka as the lord of the gods slew Vṛtra.

sanskrit: taṃ gahvare prakāśe vā pothayiṣyāmi kīcakam atha ced avabhotsyanti haṃsye matsyān api dhruvam
english: Whether in a hidden place or in the open, I will crush Kīcaka — and if anyone should discover it, I will certainly slay the Matsyas as well.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaṃ hatvā pratipatsye vasuṃdharām kāmaṃ matsyam upāstāṃ hi kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then, having slain Duryodhana, I will reclaim the earth — let Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, serve under the Matsya king as long as he likes.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca yathā na saṃtyajethās tvaṃ satyaṃ vai matkṛte vibho nigūḍhas tvaṃ tathā vīra kīcakaṃ vinipātaya
english: Draupadī said: Act so that you do not abandon your pledge of truth on my account, O mighty one — staying concealed, O hero, bring Kīcaka down in that way.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca evam etat kariṣyāmi yathā tvaṃ bhīru bhāṣase adṛśyamānas tasyādya tamasvinyām anindite
english: Bhīmasena said: I will do exactly as you say, O timid one — unseen by him, this very night in the darkness, O blameless one.

sanskrit: nāgo bilvam ivākramya pothayiṣyāmy ahaṃ śiraḥ alabhyām icchatas tasya kīcakasya durātmanaḥ
english: As an elephant tramples a bilva fruit, I will crush the head of that wicked-souled Kīcaka who desires what cannot be obtained.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhīmo 'tha prathamaṃ gatvā rātrau channa upāviśat mṛgaṃ harir ivādṛśyaḥ pratyākāṅkṣat sa kīcakam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Bhīma went first and sat concealed in the night — like a lion invisible to its prey, he waited for Kīcaka.

sanskrit: kīcakaś cāpy alaṃkṛtya yathākāmam upāvrajat tāṃ velāṃ nartanāgāre pāñcālīsaṃgamāśayā
english: And Kīcaka, having adorned himself to his heart's desire, approached that time and place at the dance hall with the hope of union with Pāñcālī.

sanskrit: manyamānaḥ sa saṃketam āgāraṃ prāviśac ca tam praviśya ca sa tad veśma tamasā saṃvṛtaṃ mahat
english: Thinking of the assignation, he entered that dwelling; and entering, he found that great hall enveloped in darkness.

sanskrit: pūrvāgataṃ tatas tatra bhīmam apratimaujasam ekāntam āsthitaṃ cainam āsasāda sudurmatiḥ
english: Then that evil-minded one encountered Bhīma of incomparable might, who had arrived first and was sitting there alone in a corner.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ śayane tatra mṛtyuṃ sūtaḥ parāmṛśat jājvalyamānaṃ kopena kṛṣṇādharṣaṇajena ha
english: The charioteer's son touched the one lying on the bed — and that one was Death itself, blazing with fury born of the insult to Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: upasaṃgamya caivainaṃ kīcakaḥ kāmamohitaḥ harṣonmathitacittātmā smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: And approaching him, Kīcaka, blinded by desire, his mind and soul churned by excitement, said with a smile:

sanskrit: prāpitaṃ te mayā vittaṃ bahurūpam anantakam tat sarvaṃ tvāṃ samuddiśya sahasā samupāgataḥ
english: 'I have provided you with wealth of many kinds and without limit — with all of that in mind for you, I have hastened here.'

sanskrit: nākasmān māṃ praśaṃsanti sadā gṛhagatāḥ striyaḥ suvāsā darśanīyaś ca nānyo 'sti tvādṛśaḥ pumān
english: 'Women who stay at home always praise me without cause — I am well-dressed and handsome, and there is no man like you,' — meaning himself.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca diṣṭyā tvaṃ darśanīyo 'si diṣṭyātmānaṃ praśaṃsasi īdṛśas tu tvayā sparśaḥ spṛṣṭapūrvo na karhi cit
english: Bhīmasena said: How fortunate that you are so handsome, how fortunate that you praise yourself — but such a touch as you are about to receive from me you have never felt before.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā taṃ mahābāhur bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ samutpatya ca kaunteyaḥ prahasya ca narādhamam bhīmo jagrāha keśeṣu mālyavatsu sugandhiṣu
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed Bhīma of terrible prowess, son of Kuntī, leapt up and laughing at that lowest of men, Bhīma seized him by the hair adorned with garlands and sweet-smelling.

sanskrit: sa keśeṣu parāmṛṣṭo balena balināṃ varaḥ ākṣipya keśān vegena bāhvor jagrāha pāṇḍavam
english: Seized by the hair by that force, Kīcaka — the best among the strong — swiftly pulled away from the hair-grip and grasped the Pāṇḍava by the arms.

sanskrit: bāhuyuddhaṃ tayor āsīt kruddhayor narasiṃhayoḥ vasante vāśitāhetor balavadgajayor iva
english: A wrestling match ensued between those two lions among men in their fury, like two mighty elephants fighting in spring over a cow in heat.

sanskrit: īṣad āgalitaṃ cāpi krodhāc calapadaṃ sthitam kīcako balavān bhīmaṃ jānubhyām ākṣipad bhuvi
english: Though slightly slipping and stepping unsteadily out of rage, the powerful Kīcaka struck Bhīma down to the ground with his knees.
